abstract: Feng, Hartline and Li (FHL) study revenue maximization for one buyer when the seller holds one sample from the buyer's value distribution, and define the revelation gap as the ratio between the best prior-independent approximation ratio of (scale-invariant) truthful mechanisms and that of all mechanisms. For monotone-hazard-rate (MHR) distributions they show that this gap lies in $[1.190, 1.467]$. Tang, Tao and Wang (TTW) recently studied a hidden-sample model in which the buyer may report her distribution; for MHR distributions they prove that no mechanism achieves a ratio better than $2/(1+2\ln 2)\approx 0.838$, and report a computer-assisted lower bound of $0.79$ for an optimal monotone hidden pricing mechanism. We show that both bounds hold in FHL's formal model (real-valued bids, interim individual rationality, payments that may depend on the sample): the impossibility transfers because every bid mechanism induces a feasible point of TTW's program (we also treat the strict reading of FHL's class, positive densities only, by a smoothing argument), and the guarantee transfers through a menu mechanism with real bids. We make TTW's $0.79$ bound rigorous with an interval-arithmetic verification covering all parameters, checked by two independently written programs. Consequently the optimal all-mechanism ratio $\beta_{\mathrm{all}}$ for MHR distributions satisfies $1/2+\ln 2 \le \beta_{\mathrm{all}} \le 1/0.79$, and for any bounds $\beta^-\le\beta_{\mathrm{rev}}\le\beta^+$ on the truthful ratio the revelation gap lies in $[0.79\,\beta^-,\ \beta^+/(1/2+\ln 2)]$. Substituting the numerical values $64.4\%$ and $64.8\%$ reported for $1/\beta_{\mathrm{rev}}$ by Allouah, Bahamou and Besbes (Operations Research 2022, Tables 1 and 3) yields $[1.21913, 1.30143]$ (compared with $[1.190,1.467]$ of FHL); outward rounding of the final calculation does not remove uncertainty in those source values, and the wider interval $[1.21819, 1.30244]$ is conservative under a nearest-$0.1\%$ rounding assumption.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Abstract and Section 1 ('On the values of beta_rev'): state explicitly that [1.21913, 1.30143] is obtained by substituting the numerical values 64.4% and 64.8% reported in Allouah, Bahamou and Besbes [5], that outward rounding of the final calculation does not remove uncertainty in those source values, and that the wider interval [1.21819, 1.30244] is conservative under a nearest-0.1% rounding assumption; replace [1.543, 1.575] = [1/0.648, 1/0.635] with an approximate relation.
- Section 1 ('On the values of beta_rev'): explain that a scale-invariant posted-price rule has a price-to-sample ratio whose distribution does not depend on the scale and therefore satisfies the well-behaved-at-zero condition of [5, Definition 1]; qualify the statement that scale invariance is without loss as holding under the hypotheses of [3, 5, Proposition 1].
title: Hidden-pricing bounds in the bid model of single-sample pricing and the MHR revelation gap
